title: A file handle with RAII
description:
Wrap `std::FILE*` so it always gets closed.

```
wrote 3 lines
read: first / second / third
closed automatically: 1 open files left -> 0
```
hints: The destructor checks `if (m_file) std::fclose(m_file);` so a moved-from object closes nothing (lesson 5.01).

`std::fopen(path, mode)` returns `nullptr` when it fails. To refuse to build the object, throw from the constructor: `if (!m_file) throw std::runtime_error{ "cannot open file" };` (from `<stdexcept>`). No object exists afterwards, so no destructor runs, and `main` can catch it with `try { ... } catch (const std::exception& e) { std::cout << e.what(); }`.
requirements: `class File` opens in the constructor (throwing `std::runtime_error` on failure) and closes in the destructor.
Copying is deleted; moving transfers the handle.
